definition: The OpenAI SDKs are the official client libraries for calling OpenAI models — chat, the Responses API, embeddings, images and audio.
details: Published and maintained by OpenAI for Python and TypeScript/JavaScript.

explainer.lead: How to install OpenAI SDK, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()   # reads OPENAI_API_KEY
resp = client.responses.create(model="gpt-4o-mini", input="Give me a one-line definition of overfitting.")
print(resp.output_text)

emb = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input="vector search")
print(len(emb.data[0].embedding))

explainer.inAi: Many other tools (vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM) expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so this SDK with a different base_url talks to them too.

tiers.eli5: It is a ready-made toolkit so your program can talk to an AI service without building the connection itself.
tiers.practitioner: Published and maintained by OpenAI for Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, so engineers call models through these libraries rather than hand-rolling requests. The pitfall is assuming the surface is the same across languages and features.
tiers.paperLevel: Official client libraries wrapping OpenAI model endpoints: chat, Responses API, embeddings, images and audio. They are maintained by OpenAI for the two stated languages.

explainer.example: A TypeScript web app and a Python script can both call chat and embeddings through their respective official SDKs instead of custom HTTP code.
